source.title: DataShield: Safety-degrading Data Filtering for LLM Benign Instruction Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Jun-Bo Zhang; Qian-Li Zhou; Xin-Yang Deng; Wen Jiang; Jie Pan; Jin-Biao Zhu

record.file_problem: Text appears to contain the full paper; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests benign instruction fine-tuning with harmful-request ASR, using new model and dataset settings; also reports token-wise KL after fine-tuning.
record.gate_note: Records the study’s benign fine-tuning ASR results, including its high-risk and low-risk DataShield-selected subsets, and its token-wise KL analysis. Cited results from other work and comparisons for other filtering methods are not recorded. Activation projections, layer-selection scores, and representation-separability results are not ASR measures; their curves are not extracted as behavioral outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-aligned instruct models on benign Alpaca and Dolly data and measures harmful-request ASR on HEx-PHI, DirectHarm4 and HarmBench. This is close to the original benign fine-tuning setup, on newer models (Llama3, Llama3.1, Qwen2.5) with LoRA, so it bears directly on V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that benign fine-tuning degrades safety by raising overall response compliance while harm recognition stays intact. A pre-fine-tuning compliance-projection score identifies high-risk benign samples, which sharply raise ASR, and low-risk samples, which keep ASR at or below the original model. Open-ended, longer-response samples (brainstorming, open/general QA) are riskiest. The KL prefix-shift claim compares fine-tuned with the original aligned model, not aligned with base.
record.recipe_differences: Benign instruction SFT and harmful-request ASR are used, with LoRA on Llama3, Llama3.1, and Qwen2.5 and Alpaca/Dolly data. The paper does not specify the original study’s fine-tuning recipe in comparable detail; this study additionally evaluates sample filtering and token-wise KL.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies by model, dataset, benchmark, and sample-risk subset. The authors state that safety performance varies substantially across models even on the same dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Token-wise KL between fine-tuned and original aligned models on HEx-PHI. The shift is large and concentrated in initial prefix tokens after high-risk benign fine-tuning, and minimal after low-risk fine-tuning (figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning that erodes safety shifts the aligned model's output distribution mainly at the first response tokens.

fits_no_version.finding: After benign fine-tuning, harmful and benign prompts stay separable in activation space. Projections onto a compliance direction rise much more than harmfulness-perception projections (Figs. 4–5, Llama3-8B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning erodes safety by raising general compliance rather than impairing harm recognition.

record.problems: The token-wise KL results are figure-only with no numerical values or uncertainty reported. ASR tables report no uncertainty estimates. The paper notes substantial model- and dataset-dependent safety outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted the Table I Random results and other filtering-method comparisons, which are method comparisons rather than the study’s own DataShield intervention. Also omitted layer-wise filtering curves in Figures 8–10; the tabled top/bottom subset results are retained. Activation-projection and representation-separability measures are not harmful-compliance rates.

untested.parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning is run; Pure-Bad is used only to extract the compliance vector.

Only LoRA rank 8 is tested, on 7–8B open models, with Alpaca and Dolly. Full-parameter fine-tuning, closed or API models, other benign datasets, and dose versus sample count beyond 1,000 and 8,000 samples are not tested.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL is reported. The only KL compares fine-tuned with aligned models and is figure-only.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attack.
Picks a 'safety-critical' activation layer for scoring. It does not test whether few weights or ranks carry safety.

missing.what: Random 1,000-sample benign fine-tuning ASR, the most direct 'ordinary benign data' test. It rises on DirectHarm4 and HarmBench for all models (e.g. Llama3 Alpaca 12.75→36.75). On HEx-PHI it falls below baseline for Llama3.1 (7.93→5.17) and Qwen2.5 (10.69→9.31), so it is benchmark-dependent.
Fine-tuning on the 80% of data retained after DataShield filtering still leaves ASR well above baseline, e.g. Llama3 Dolly DirectHarm4 60.00 vs 12.75.
missing.locator: Table III, '+ Ours' rows; Section V-D

missing.what: Layer-wise top/bottom-1000 ASR curves on Dolly (top subsets spike ASR at most layers).

record.verdict_notes: Qi et al. 2310.03693 is cited as [5]; this study is not an original source. The V3 rows were unlinked because the KL measure compares fine-tuned with aligned models, not aligned with base. Both the top-1000 and bottom-1000 subsets come from the paper's own ranking method, but they are still benign fine-tuning outcomes on harmful-request ASR. ASR is judged by Llama-Guard-3-8B with no uncertainty reported. Random-column values are identical across Alpaca and Dolly on HEx-PHI for each model, which may be a reporting error.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning intervention is reported.
Tests benign Alpaca and Dolly fine-tuning and DataShield-selected subsets on three models; does not test all ordinary or carefully selected benign-data recipes.
Reports KL between benign-fine-tuned models and the original aligned models on HEx-PHI, not a general aligned-versus-base comparison.
No compliant-prefix prefilling, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change experiment.
Identifies safety-critical activation layers but does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not test whether the data or training objective causes safety to be shallow.
No training intervention intended to deepen safety or test its durability.

relationships.condition: Unfiltered fine-tuning on 10k Alpaca or Dolly samples for Llama3.1 and Qwen2.5, plus Llama3 on Dolly (Table III)
relationships.reason: ASR rises from about 4–13% to 34–84% on all three benchmarks (r4–r18). Llama3 Alpaca HarmBench also rises, 3.5→21.5 (r2).
relationships.display_finding: Attack success rose from about 4–13% to 34–84% on all three benchmarks, and Llama3 on Alpaca also rose on HarmBench, from 3.5 to 21.5.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Unfiltered fine-tuning on 10k Alpaca or Dolly samples for Llama3.1 and Qwen2.5, plus Llama3 on Dolly (Table III)
source_check.reason: Table III confirms the large ASR increases in r4–r18; r2 also shows increased harmful compliance.

relationships.condition: Fine-tuning on the 1,000 benign samples DataShield ranks as highest risk, all three models and both datasets (Table I)
relationships.reason: Selected benign subsets raise ASR well above the instruct baseline, e.g. Llama3 Dolly HEx-PHI 5.86→91.00 (r19–r36).
relationships.display_finding: The selected benign subsets raised attack success far above the instruct baseline, for example from 5.86 to 91.00 on HEx-PHI for Llama3 on Dolly.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Fine-tuning on the 1,000 benign samples DataShield ranks as highest risk, all three models and both datasets (Table I)
source_check.reason: Table I shows increased ASR over the instruct baseline across all six model-dataset combinations, including r19–r25.

relationships.reason: Increases are modest (DirectHarm4 12.75→23.75, HEx-PHI 5.86→14.83). Authors say there is no obvious safety drop, so the effect depends on model and dataset (r1, r3).
relationships.display_finding: After full Alpaca fine-tuning of Llama3-8B-Instruct, increases were modest (DirectHarm4 12.75 to 23.75, HEx-PHI 5.86 to 14.83), and the authors see no obvious safety drop.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Table III gives smaller increases for r1 and r3 than for the other model-dataset settings; Section V-D explicitly describes this setting as lacking an obvious safety drop.

relationships.condition: Fine-tuning on the 1,000 benign samples ranked lowest risk (Table II)
relationships.reason: ASR falls below the instruct baseline in most settings (r37–r51, r54). Qwen2.5 Dolly shows only a tiny rise (r52, r53). Whether benign data erodes safety depends on which samples are used.
relationships.display_finding: Fine-tuning on the 1,000 lowest-risk benign samples cut ASR below the instruct baseline in most settings, e.g. 12.75% to 1.50% and 5.86% to 0.34%, while Qwen2.5 on Dolly showed only small rises (9.50% to 10.20% and 6.50% to 8.50%).

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Fine-tuning on the 1,000 benign samples ranked lowest risk (Table II)
source_check.reason: Table II shows reversed effects in r37–r51 and r54, including r37: 12.75%→1.50% and r39: 5.86%→0.34%. These warrant challenges. Split off Qwen2.5 Dolly DirectHarm4 and Harmbench, whose small increases, 9.50%→10.20% and 6.50%→8.50%, warrant limits_scope.
